defaults.permitted_development: A modest porch on a house in England is usually permitted development where the external ground-floor area does not exceed 3 square metres, no part is more than 3m above ground level and no part is within 2m of the highway boundary. Local conditions or Article 4 directions can still remove that fallback.

rules.height_rules: The key height limit is 3m overall, measured in the same way as a house extension. There is no extra allowance for a pitched, vaulted or feature porch roof once it exceeds that height.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate projection allowance. The main size test is the external ground-floor area, which should not exceed 3 square metres including wall thickness.
rules.boundary_rules: No part of the porch should be within 2m of any boundary between the dwellinghouse and the highway. On tight front plots this setback test is often the deciding issue.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof allowance beyond the 3 square metre footprint and 3m height cap. Any porch roof design has to sit within those same limits.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials that match or complement the host house so the porch reads as part of the entrance rather than a bolt-on box. Heritage settings often call for the closest material match and more restrained detailing.

rules.permitted_development: The normal porch route is quite tight: up to 3 square metres externally, up to 3 metres high and set at least 2 metres back from the highway boundary. Anything larger is treated more like an extension.

rules.height_rules: A porch above 3 metres in height will normally require planning permission.
rules.depth_rules: Porches are controlled by external footprint rather than by a simple projection away from the front wall.
rules.boundary_rules: No part of the porch should be within 2 metres of any boundary between the dwellinghouse and the highway. This includes roads, pavements and other adjoining highways.
rules.roof_rules: Flat and pitched porch roofs are both possible if the whole structure stays within the normal caps. A decorative roof does not create extra planning allowance.
rules.materials_rules: Because a porch is usually prominent from the street, material matching and restrained detailing often matter as much as the size limits.

restrictions.conservation_area: Additional planning restrictions may apply in conservation areas.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent is required for works affecting listed buildings.
restrictions.article4_notes: No borough-wide Article 4 note is recorded here, but site-specific directions or planning conditions can still remove permitted development rights on particular properties.

rules.permitted_development: The normal porch route is quite tight: up to 3 square metres externally, up to 3 metres high and set at least 2 metres back from the highway boundary. Anything larger is treated more like an extension.

rules.height_rules: A porch that looks modest in footprint can still lose the benefit of the ordinary route if it becomes too tall.
rules.depth_rules: Porch with an external ground-floor area above 3 square metres will normally need planning permission.
rules.boundary_rules: No part of the porch should be within 2 metres of any boundary between the dwellinghouse and the highway. This includes roads, pavements and other adjoining highways.
rules.roof_rules: Roof designs that make the porch exceed the standard height or footprint limits will normally need planning permission.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials that sit naturally with the existing house, especially on the front elevation where the porch is usually read as part of the main entrance composition.
